latest_census.notes: 5th Population and Housing Census, 2008 (pre-secession; ~30.9 million counted in the north). The UNSD country paper 'The Fifth population census in Sudan' (https://unstats.un.org/unsd/demographic/sources/census/countries/SDN.pdf) and the IHSN catalogue entry (https://catalog.ihsn.org/index.php/catalog/4216) say: 'Based on the understanding that ethnicity and religion are causes of conflicts in Sudan, the Presidency decided to delete these questions', despite the South Sudan Population Census Council insisting on re-inclusion; the south cited 'the north's veto of ethnicity and religion on the census questionnaires' (Al Jazeera, 2008-04-14). Design: a short form (11 questions) for 90% of EAs and a long form for 10%. Whether the long form asked mother tongue could not be established -- no snippet mentioned language, and the IPUMS variable-list search was not run (budget exhausted). The 1955/56 First Population Census is described in results as 'the only census that recorded ethnicity' (HRW appendix; Sudan Embassy Beijing 'Tribal composition' page), tabulated by the nine provinces of the time.

subnational_sources.evidence: Snippet: '720 Clusters (40 per state) and 18,000 Households (1,000 per state) to ensure adequate representation of statistical estimation by each state' -- i.e. designed as a state-level estimation domain, unlike Afrobarometer. Standard MICS household questionnaires carry religion of household head, but no result confirmed that Sudan's did or that a by-state religion table is in the report; the snippet only said the cross-tabulation 'was not directly displayed'. Microdata: https://microdata.worldbank.org/index.php/catalog/2656 (registration). Survey, so ranked below any count; would supersede the 4 Afrobarometer admin1 rows and needs owner review.

subnational_sources.evidence: Search result title 'APPENDIX A: POPULATION OF SUDAN: ETHNIC CENSUS OF 1956 (ONLY ...'; snippets say the 1956 census 'was the only census that recorded ethnicity' and was 'organized around nine provinces'. Seventy years old, pre-secession, and on a province set that fits neither level: a historical note at best, not a fill. The original 'First Population Census of Sudan, 1955/56. Supplement to Interim Reports' is catalogued on Google Books (https://books.google.com/books/about/First_Population_Census_of_Sudan_1955_56.html?id=JpIUAQAAMAAJ) with interim tables for 'Khartoum, Kassala, Darfur, and other regions'.

tier_reason: The 2008 census did not ask religion or ethnicity -- the Presidency deleted both questions (UNSD country paper, IHSN). The only count that ever recorded ethnicity is the 1956 census, on 9 pre-secession provinces that match neither the 19 admin1 nor the 189 admin2 shapes. Language on the 2008 long form is unestablished. The nearest thing to subnational religion is the MICS 2014 survey, designed for state-level estimation, unconfirmed for the field and behind a PDF/registration -- a B-grade survey route, not a count.
recommended_action: Declare religion and ethnicity `not_collected` for the 2008 census with the UNSD/IHSN evidence, keeping the existing Afrobarometer R9 survey rows (religion, 4 of 19 admin1; ethnicity was not asked in Sudan, code 9994). If the owner wants survey religion for all states, open the MICS 2014 final report PDF and check for a religion-of-household-head by state table before touching the microdata; that would supersede the Afrobarometer rows and needs review. Separately, resolve why the boundary file draws 19 admin1 against 18 states. Leave the 1956 ethnic census as a historical note only. Already closed and not re-researched: the USCB/HDX Sudan workbook (nationality only, docs/SOURCES.md).

summary: Sudan's last census (2008) deliberately dropped religion and ethnicity: the Presidency deleted both questions as conflict-sensitive, over the South's objection, so no census count of either exists for any of the 19 states or 189 localities; whether the 10% long form asked language could not be established. The only ethnic count ever taken is the 1955/56 census on nine pre-secession provinces, reproduced as a PDF appendix by HRW, which fits neither boundary level. The best subnational religion candidate is the CBS/UNICEF MICS 2014 survey, which was designed to estimate by state (18 states, 1,000 households each), but no result confirmed a religion table and it sits in a PDF report and registration-gated microdata; it would supersede the four Afrobarometer rows now on the map. Tier C: declare religion and ethnicity not_collected for the 2008 census with the evidence above, and treat MICS as an optional survey route for owner review. The Wikipedia checks and the CBS-site search were not run because the session's search budget ran out.
